item.title: This little brown mushroom is laced with a hallucinogen — and lethal toxins
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03639-2

A Florida fungus might combine the psychedelic compound psilocybin with deadly chemicals to defend itself against hungry animals.

item.title: Record-breaking Ebola outbreak: phone data reconstruct first weeks of spread
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03666-z

The Bundibugyo virus strain was circulating for weeks before its detection in May, but was missed owing to surveillance failures, testing gaps and funding cuts, researchers say.
item.dc:title: Record-breaking Ebola outbreak: phone data reconstruct first weeks of spread
item.dc:creator: Mohana Basu

item.title: Massive atlas of brain region linked to a host of diseases is the most detailed yet
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03565-3

A global team profiled nearly 26 million brain cells from the basal ganglia to build a cross-species reference database that will help to understand conditions from Parkinson’s disease to addiction.
item.dc:title: Massive atlas of brain region linked to a host of diseases is the most detailed yet
item.dc:creator: Miryam Naddaf

item.title: RSV vaccines slash infections: data show jabs’ staggering success against dangerous virus
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03573-3

Vaccines and monoclonal-antibody injections are cutting hospitalizations linked to the respiratory virus.
item.dc:title: RSV vaccines slash infections: data show jabs’ staggering success against dangerous virus
item.dc:creator: Liam Drew

item.content:encoded:

item.dc:creator: Heidi Ledford

item.title: Daily briefing: Should old, bad science be culled from the literature?
item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03675-y

AI tools that summarize scientific literature are picking up decades-old flawed papers — should they be retracted? Plus, the first image of a black hole holds up to scrutiny and how the Artemis II mission might have disrupted GPS.
item.dc:title: Daily briefing: Should old, bad science be culled from the literature?
item.dc:creator: Flora Graham
